notes.title: Business model
notes.text: Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, and sells related services.

notes.title: Fiscal comparability
notes.text: FY2024 and FY2022 each contained 52 weeks; FY2023 contained 53 weeks. Growth comparisons are not normalized for the additional week.

notes.title: Services growth
notes.anchor: advertising, the App Store and cloud services
notes.text: Management attributes FY2024 Services growth primarily to advertising, the App Store and cloud services.

notes.title: Greater China
notes.text: Management attributes the Greater China revenue decline primarily to lower iPhone sales; renminbi weakness also had an unfavorable effect.

notes.title: Margin drivers
notes.text: Management cites cost savings for the improvement in Products gross margin, partly offset by product mix and foreign exchange. Services gross margin percentage increased due to a different Services mix.

notes.title: Tax comparability
notes.text: Apple reported a one-time income-tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the State Aid Decision. Reported GAAP net income is shown without an adjusted-income substitute.

notes.title: Restricted funds
notes.text: Funds to settle the State Aid Decision obligation were held in escrow and restricted from general use. Balance-sheet cash plus marketable securities is not the same as unrestricted liquidity.

notes.title: Capital allocation
notes.text: In May 2024 Apple announced a share-repurchase authorization of up to $110 billion. An authorization is distinct from actual cash repurchases in the cash-flow statement.

notes.title: Risk context
notes.text: Apple describes highly competitive markets, aggressive pricing, short product life cycles and rapidly changing technology. This historical review does not forecast returns or provide a stock-price target.
